guidelines.detail: documentation rule GW-06 not applied (The description specifies reporting duties with separate applicability tests, and the missing flows show that the reporting paths and their reconnection were not modeled. Several duties may apply to the same accident, supporting an inclusive split and join. Documented guideline GW-06 already states this gateway pattern.)

same as LRN-015 (The description distinguishes reporting duties by recipient and reporting circumstances, while some generated labels do not preserve the corresponding decision meaning. This is already captured by the learned guideline LRN-015 on preserving stated semantics in element labels.)

same as LRN-030 (The description distinguishes incident types and separate reporting criteria, while the cited missing flows show that the corresponding decision branches and actions were not connected. This is already covered in substance by learned guideline LRN-030.)

same as LRN-037 (The description distinguishes reporting actions and decisions by their scope, severity, timing, and eligibility, while the generated labels broaden or omit some of those distinctions. This is essentially the same label-preservation guidance as LRN-037.)

same as LRN-003 (The description identifies distinct kinds of occurrences and different reporting obligations, while the reference routes the flow after notification according to occurrence type. The missing gateway and branch flows support modeling that selection. This is essentially the learned rule to model a choice with an appropriate gateway.)

same as LRN-015 (The description ties the reporting condition to both a fatality and insured status (S8), while the generated gateway label omits the insured-status distinction (P3). This is already covered by learned guideline LRN-015.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states multiple reporting duties, each activated by a separate test, and permits several to apply together.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states the action, purpose, recipient, scope, or outcome of a process element: Label the corresponding BPMN element with a concise phrase that preserves those stated semantics; do not substitute a related but different meaning, omit distinguishing details, or add unsupported details.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description distinguishes process elements by their actions, recipients, scope, or outcomes

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description distinguishes mutually exclusive cases by conditions, assigns different actions to them, and later gives them a shared continuation: Model the case selection with an exclusive split, and reconverge the alternative paths with an exclusive merge before the shared continuation.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description distinguishes mutually exclusive case types and assigns different subsequent actions to them.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description distinguishes multiple activities or events by their action, information, or outcome: Label each corresponding BPMN element to preserve those distinctions, rather than using interchangeable or overly generic labels.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description distinguishes an activity or decision by a criterion that changes what is done or decided

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that one of several alternatives is selected, or that an activity may occur: Model the choice or optional activity with an appropriate gateway, and reconnect the resulting paths before subsequent common work.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies multiple kinds of occurrences and specifies different follow-up actions for those kinds
